title: What is known about 1RB0LD_0LC0RE_1LA0RD_0RB0LF_1RC1LA_0RB---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LD_0LC0RE_1LA0RD_0RB0LF_1RC1LA_0RB---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.

Mirrored and with its states renamed, this machine has the engine of 1RB0LE_1LC0RE_0RA0LD_1LA0LF_0LC0RA_0RE--- and the F02 two-word sweepers: a base-3 counter N with 3-cell digits at the right end (the wall of 110s of the first look is made of its top digits), binary counters with 4-cell digits on the left, and an undecoded middle between them. The laws of N and of the binary streams are proved in Lean for every size.
verdict: The question is open. No halt in LONGRUN_STEPS steps of the C simulator; Lean proves no halt in the first 107 steps (native_decide) and the laws of the outer parts of the tape for every size.

Where a halt would come from. Only F1 halts and F is entered only from D reading 1 (0LF), millions of times (3,571,420 in 108 steps), always with a 0 left of D. The rare transition is E1 (66 times in 108 steps), the counterpart of the rare D1 events of its relative.
What is missing. The rules of the middle part, and an invariant explaining why D never reads 1 next to a 1.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: The halting pattern never forms
claims.text: F is entered only from D reading 1, 3,571,420 times in the first 10<sup>8</sup> steps, always with a 0 left of D, so F reads 0.

claims.title: The base-3 counter N, for every size
claims.text: Read the cells right of N's low end three at a time from the head outward, 010 = 0, 110 = 1, 100 = 2, blank beyond. A visit in state C adds one; it comes back out in A without carry and in D with a carry; a carry through all digits makes the blank into a new digit 2.

claims.title: The binary streams, for every size
claims.text: The stream laws of the F02 sibling 1RB0LE_1LC0RE_0RA0LD_1LA1LF_0LC0RA_0LB--- hold for the mirror image of this machine with its states renamed (C, A, B, E, D as the sibling's A, B, C, D, E): a visit in state A to an a/z stream on the left is a binary increment, a visit in state C to the counter M adds one and wraps.

claims.title: The run uses the counter law
claims.text: In the run, the cells right of 126 are entered only in state C, and all 142,058 of those visits, from step 689,712 to step 43,905,102, are rows of the counter law; then the middle reaches 126 and N's low end moves outward. At 10<sup>9</sup> steps N fills cells 149 to 191 (15 digits).

claims.title: Three parts of the tape
claims.text: The crossing profile at 10<sup>9</sup> steps: ×1/3 every 3 cells going right over 149 to 191 (N), no pattern over 62 to 149 (the middle), ×2 every 4 cells going right over 22 to 62 (binary counters with 4-cell digits), a few hundred over -46 to 22.

claims.title: No halt in the first 30,000,000,000 steps
claims.text: The C simulator runs 30,000,000,000 steps from blank tape without a halt; at the end cells -50 to 213 (264 cells), 118 ones.

claims.title: The mirror of a relative
claims.text: Mirrored and renamed, the table is 1RB0LE_1LC0RE_0RA0LD_1LA1RB_0LC0RF_0LC---, which shares the prefix 1RB0LE_1LC0RE_0RA0LD_1LA with 1RB0LE_1LC0RE_0RA0LD_1LA0LF_0LC0RA_0RE---; most of its configurations in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps occur, mirrored, in that machine's run (holdouts/related.json).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Needed: the rules of the middle part and of the rare E1 events, then why D never reads 1 next to a 1.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same tapes at another pace, whatever the states, as 1 other holdout (listed on the explainer page).

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this machine runs a base-3 counter at its right end and binary counters at its left, both proved in Lean, with a middle part between them that nobody has decoded yet. This page runs the real machine in your browser and lists what is known.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 264 cells visited.
The base-3 counter and the binary streams, proved for every size.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
Where the time goes and the rare events start; not decoded.

sections.heading: A relative in a mirror
html: Mirror the tape and rename the states (C, A, B, E, D, F as A, B, C, D, E, F): the table becomes 1RB0LE_1LC0RE_0RA0LD_1LA1RB_0LC0RF_0LC---, which shares the prefix 1RB0LE_1LC0RE_0RA0LD_1LA with 1RB0LE_1LC0RE_0RA0LD_1LA0LF_0LC0RA_0RE--- and the F02 two-word sweepers. So it is the same cascade of counters, seen in a mirror: the base-3 counter at the right end and the binary streams on the left. The crossing profile (c/cross.c, 109 steps, cells -46 to 192):

sections.heading: The right counter
html: The right counter N (proved). Read the cells right of N's low end three at a time from the head outward: 010 = 0, 110 = 1, 100 = 2; blank beyond. A visit in state C adds one; it comes back out in state A (no carry) or D (carry); a carry through every digit turns blank cells into a new digit 2. lean/Counter.lean proves it for every number of digits (n_inc0, n_inc1, n_inc0_carry, n_inc1_carry, n_overflow), from five rows (lean/VisitR.lean, predicate Vis). In the run, the cells right of 126 are entered only in state C and all 142,058 of those visits are these rows, from step 689,712 until step 43,905,102 (c/vislaws.c); then the middle reaches 126 and N's low end moves outward. The wall of 110s at the right end is made of N's top digits.

sections.heading: The binary streams on the left
html: The binary streams (proved). lean/Stream.lean proves the stream laws of the F02 sibling 1RB0LE_1LC0RE_0RA0LD_1LA1LF_0LC0RA_0LB--- for the mirror image of this machine with the states renamed (predicate VisL, streams left of the head, nearest cell first): a visit in state A (the sibling's B) to an a/z stream is a binary increment (vb_odd, vb_even, ve_odd), a visit in state C (the sibling's A) to the counter M adds one and wraps (m_inc, m_wrap). From 29 token rows mined left of cell 30 (lean/VisitL.lean).

sections.heading: Where it could halt
html: Where it could halt. Only F1 halts, and F is entered only from D reading 1 (0LF), which is frequent here: 3,571,420 times in the first 108 steps, always with a 0 left of D, so F reads 0 and goes on with 0RB. In the renamed table this is the step E1 = 0RF followed by F0 = 0LC; the relatives have E1 = 0RA or 0RE there. The rare transition is E1 (1LA, the renamed D1 = 1RB): 66 times in 108 steps, the counterpart of the rare D1 events of 1RB0LE_1LC0RE_0RA0LD_1LA0LF_0LC0RA_0RE---. holdouts/related.json already notes that most of this machine's configurations in its first 107 steps also occur, mirrored, in the run of that machine.

sections.heading: What is left
html:
• Decode the middle (cells 62 to 149 at 109 steps).
  • Why D never reads 1 with a 1 to its left (millions of times per 108 steps): a local invariant that no CTL window up to 8 cells captures; it should follow from the decoded layout.

• Direct C simulation (c/longrun.c): 30,000,000,000 steps, no halt; at the end cells -50 to 213 (264 cells), 118 ones.
  • No macro-level accelerator: the time is spent in the undecoded middle.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 239 cells (46 left of the start, 192 right), with a density of 1s of 0.431.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same tapes at another pace (observed, not proved). Leave the states aside and compare only the tape and the place of the head. Then a large part of the first 107 configurations of this machine are configurations of the machines below, in the same order and up to the end of the run. The steps at which they occur differ, the tables are not renamings of each other, and equal tapes with different states may be continued differently, so this does not tie the halting questions together.

  • 1RB0LE_1LC0RE_0RA0LD_1LA0LF_0LC0RA_0RE--- (in a mirror): 9,285,736 configurations, the last at step 10,000,000 here and step 9,285,895 there

family: F02 engine with a different D1/F path: counters behind a growing middle
summary: The mirror image of a relative of 1RB0LE_1LC0RE_0RA0LD_1LA0LF_0LC0RA_0RE---: a base-3 counter at the right end and binary counters at the left (both proved in Lean for every size), with an undecoded middle.
